ladder.title: Sumsets of integers: the trivial bound and its equality case
ladder.q:
Let $A$ be a finite nonempty set of integers and $A+A=\{a+b : a,b\in A\}$. Prove that $$|A+A|\ge 2|A|-1.$$

Show moreover that equality holds if and only if $A$ is an arithmetic progression.
ladder.source: M. B. Nathanson, Additive Number Theory: Inverse Problems and the Geometry of Sumsets, GTM 165, Springer (1996), Ch. 1
ladder.note: The simplest direct theorem together with its inverse theorem: extremal sumset size forces arithmetic structure.

ladder.title: The Cauchy–Davenport theorem
ladder.q: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A,B$ be nonempty subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Prove that $$|A+B|\ge \min\big(p,\ |A|+|B|-1\big).$$
ladder.source: A.-L. Cauchy (1813); H. Davenport, On the addition of residue classes, J. London Math. Soc. 10 (1935)
ladder.note: Transfers the integer bound to a cyclic group of prime order, where wrap-around is the only obstruction.

ladder.title: Ruzsa's triangle inequality
ladder.q:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite nonempty subsets of an abelian group. Prove that $$|A|\,|B-C|\le |A-B|\,|A-C|.$$

Deduce that $d(X,Y)=\log\dfrac{|X-Y|}{\sqrt{|X|\,|Y|}}$ satisfies $d(B,C)\le d(A,B)+d(A,C)$.
ladder.source: I. Z. Ruzsa (1978); T. Tao and V. Vu, Additive Combinatorics, Cambridge University Press (2006)
ladder.note: First tool for passing information about one sumset to another; an injection argument rather than a counting identity.

ladder.title: Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality
ladder.q: Let $A,B$ be finite nonempty subsets of an abelian group with $|A+B|\le K|A|$. Prove that for all integers $m,n\ge 0$ with $m+n\ge 1$, $$|mB-nB|\le K^{m+n}|A|,$$ where $mB-nB$ is the set of all $b_1+\cdots+b_m-b'_1-\cdots-b'_n$ with $b_i,b'_j\in B$.
ladder.source: G. Petridis, New proofs of Plünnecke-type estimates for product sets in groups, Combinatorica 32 (2012), 721–733 (inequality due to Plünnecke 1970 and Ruzsa 1989)
ladder.note: Small doubling propagates to all iterated sum and difference sets with polynomial loss; used in every Freiman-type theorem below.

ladder.title: Bogolyubov's lemma in the finite field model
ladder.q: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have density $\alpha=|A|/2^n>0$. Prove that $A+A+A+A$ contains a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of codimension at most $\alpha^{-2}$.
ladder.source: N. N. Bogolyubov (1939); B. Green, Finite field models in additive combinatorics, Surveys in Combinatorics 2005, LMS Lecture Note Series 327, §10
ladder.note: The basic Fourier-analytic argument (large spectrum plus Parseval); Green's Problem 50 asks to improve the codimension from $\alpha^{-2}$ to $O(\log(1/\alpha))$.

ladder.title: The Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture for restricted sums
ladder.q: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ be nonempty. Writing $A\hat{+}A=\{a+b : a,b\in A,\ a\neq b\}$, prove that $$|A\hat{+}A|\ge \min\big(p,\ 2|A|-3\big).$$
ladder.source: J. A. Dias da Silva and Y. O. Hamidoune, Cyclic spaces for Grassmann derivatives and additive theory, Bull. London Math. Soc. 26 (1994); polynomial-method proof: N. Alon, M. B. Nathanson and I. Z. Ruzsa, Adding distinct congruence classes modulo a prime, Amer. Math. Monthly 102 (1995)
ladder.note: Restricting to distinct summands breaks the Cauchy–Davenport proofs; the polynomial method handles it and settles Erdős Problem 476.

ladder.title: Freiman's 3k−4 theorem
ladder.q: Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}$ be finite with $|A|=k\ge 3$ and $$|A+A|\le 3k-4.$$ Prove that $A$ is contained in an arithmetic progression of length at most $|A+A|-k+1$.
ladder.source: G. A. Freiman (1959); see M. B. Nathanson, Additive Number Theory: Inverse Problems and the Geometry of Sumsets, GTM 165 (1996), Ch. 1
ladder.note: The first genuinely structural inverse theorem: doubling below 3 forces containment in a short progression.

ladder.title: Ruzsa's Freiman theorem in groups of exponent 2
ladder.q: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be nonempty with $|A+A|\le K|A|$. Prove that $A$ is contained in a subspace $H\le\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $$|H|\le K^2\,2^{K^4}\,|A|.$$
ladder.source: I. Z. Ruzsa, An analog of Freiman's theorem in groups, Astérisque 258 (1999), 323–326 (proved there for groups of torsion $r$, with bound $K^2r^{K^4}|A|$)
ladder.note: Freiman's theorem in the model setting with an exponential loss in $K$; Marton's conjecture (Green's Problem 49) asks for polynomial loss.

ladder.title: Sanders' quasi-polynomial Bogolyubov lemma
ladder.q: Prove that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that the following holds. If $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ has density $\alpha>0$, then $A+A+A+A$ contains a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of codimension at most $C\log^4(2/\alpha)$.
ladder.source: T. Sanders, On the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma, Analysis & PDE 5 (2012), 627–655, arXiv:1011.0107 (Theorem A.1)
ladder.note: Replaces $\alpha^{-2}$ by a power of $\log(1/\alpha)$ via almost-periodicity; the conjectured codimension in Green's Problem 50 is $O(\log(1/\alpha))$.

ladder.title: Marton's conjecture (polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa) over F_2
ladder.q: Prove that there is an absolute constant $C$ (one may take $C=12$) such that the following holds. If $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is nonempty with $|A+A|\le K|A|$, then $A$ is covered by at most $2K^{C}$ cosets of some subgroup $H\le\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|H|\le|A|$.
ladder.source: W. T. Gowers, B. Green, F. Manners and T. Tao, On a conjecture of Marton, Ann. of Math. 201 (2025), 515–549, arXiv:2311.05762 (2023)
ladder.note: Polynomial dependence on $K$, solving Green's Problem 49; its Bogolyubov-type analogue (Problem 50) remains open.

ladder.title: Schur's theorem with an explicit bound
ladder.q: Let $k\ge1$ and $N\ge\lfloor e\cdot k!\rfloor$. Prove that for every colouring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $k$ colours there exist $x,y,z$ of the same colour (not necessarily distinct) with $x+y=z$.
ladder.source: I. Schur (1916); R. L. Graham, B. L. Rothschild and J. H. Spencer, Ramsey Theory, 2nd ed., Wiley (1990)
ladder.note: Reduces to multicolour Ramsey numbers of triangles via the colouring of pairs by differences; gives the factorial upper bound in Erdős Problem 483.

ladder.title: The Schur number S(3) = 13
ladder.q: Show that $\{1,\ldots,13\}$ can be coloured with $3$ colours so that no colour class contains $x,y,z$ (not necessarily distinct) with $x+y=z$, but that every $3$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,14\}$ contains such a monochromatic solution.
ladder.source: B. M. Landman and A. Robertson, Ramsey Theory on the Integers, AMS Student Mathematical Library (2004)
ladder.note: An exact small case, showing how far the general factorial bound is from the truth.

ladder.title: Exponential lower bound for Schur numbers
ladder.q: Let $S(k)$ be the largest $N$ such that $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ admits a $k$-colouring with no monochromatic solution of $x+y=z$ ($x,y$ not necessarily distinct). Prove that $S(k+1)\ge 3S(k)+1$ for every $k\ge1$, and deduce that $$S(k)\ge\frac{3^k-1}{2}.$$
ladder.source: I. Schur (1916); R. L. Graham, B. L. Rothschild and J. H. Spencer, Ramsey Theory, 2nd ed., Wiley (1990)
ladder.note: The matching lower-bound construction; Erdős Problem 483 asks whether the true growth is exponential, i.e. whether $S(k)<c^k$.

ladder.title: Colourings that defeat a non-regular linear equation
ladder.q:
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ be nonzero integers such that $\sum_{i\in I}a_i\neq0$ for every nonempty $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$, and let $p$ be a prime with $p>\sum_{i=1}^k|a_i|$. Colour each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ by the last nonzero digit of $n$ in base $p$.

Prove that this colouring with $p-1$ colours has no monochromatic solution of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=0$.
ladder.source: R. Rado, Studien zur Kombinatorik, Math. Z. 36 (1933); R. L. Graham, B. L. Rothschild and J. H. Spencer, Ramsey Theory, 2nd ed. (1990)
ladder.note: The necessity half of Rado's theorem; the number of colours depends on the size of the coefficients, and Green's Problem 21 asks whether it can be bounded in terms of $k$ alone.

ladder.title: Van der Waerden's theorem
ladder.q: Prove that for all integers $k,r\ge1$ there exists $N$ such that every colouring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $r$ colours contains a monochromatic arithmetic progression of length $k$.
ladder.source: B. L. van der Waerden, Beweis einer Baudetschen Vermutung, Nieuw Arch. Wisk. 15 (1927)
ladder.note: The colour-focusing induction, the engine behind Rado's sufficiency proof and finite-sums theorems.

ladder.title: Folkman's finite sums theorem
ladder.q: Prove that for all integers $r,m\ge1$ there exists $N$ such that for every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ there is a set $S$ of $m$ distinct positive integers such that all sums $\sum_{s\in T}s$, over nonempty $T\subseteq S$, lie in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and have the same colour.
ladder.source: J. Folkman, R. Rado, J. Sanders; R. L. Graham, B. L. Rothschild and J. H. Spencer, Ramsey Theory, 2nd ed., Wiley (1990)
ladder.note: Finite version of Hindman's theorem; Erdős Problem 532 is the infinite version for two colours.

ladder.title: Rado's theorem for a single equation
ladder.q: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ be nonzero integers. Prove that every finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits a monochromatic solution $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ of $$a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=0$$ if and only if $\sum_{i\in I}a_i=0$ for some nonempty $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$.
ladder.source: R. Rado, Studien zur Kombinatorik, Math. Z. 36 (1933)
ladder.note: Completes the characterisation of partition regular single equations; the boundedness question in Green's Problem 21 concerns the complementary case.

ladder.title: Rado's boundedness conjecture for three variables
ladder.q: Let $a_1,a_2,a_3$ be nonzero integers such that $\sum_{i\in I}a_i\neq0$ for every nonempty $I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$. Prove that $\mathbb{N}$ can be coloured with $24$ colours so that there is no monochromatic solution of $$a_1x_1+a_2x_2+a_3x_3=0.$$
ladder.source: J. Fox and D. J. Kleitman, On Rado's boundedness conjecture, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 113 (2006), 84–100
ladder.note: The case $k=3$ of Green's Problem 21 with a bound independent of the coefficients; open for $k\ge4$.

ladder.title: Monochromatic x, x+y and xy
ladder.q: Prove that for every finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $x$, $x+y$ and $xy$ all have the same colour.
ladder.source: J. Moreira, Monochromatic sums and products in N, Ann. of Math. 185 (2017), 1069–1090
ladder.note: Forces a sum and a product into one colour (together with $x$); Green's Problem 22 asks the same for the pair $x+y$, $xy$ alone (with $x,y\ge3$ to exclude $2+2=2\cdot2$), which remains open.

ladder.title: Partition regularity of Pythagorean pairs
ladder.q: Prove that for every finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist distinct $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$ of the same colour such that $x^2+y^2$ is a perfect square.
ladder.source: N. Frantzikinakis, O. Klurman and J. Moreira, Partition regularity of Pythagorean pairs, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e5, arXiv:2309.10636
ladder.note: Settles Green's Problem 23 via multiplicative functions; partition regularity of $x^2+y^2=z^2$ with $x,y,z$ all of one colour remains open for general finite colourings.

ladder.title: Discrepancy 1 survives exactly to length 11
ladder.q:
For $f:\{1,\ldots,N\}\to\{-1,1\}$ let $D(f)=\max\{|\sum_{k=1}^{n}f(kd)| : n,d\ge1,\ nd\le N\}$.

Show that some $f:\{1,\ldots,11\}\to\{-1,1\}$ has $D(f)=1$, but that every $f:\{1,\ldots,12\}\to\{-1,1\}$ has $D(f)\ge2$.
ladder.source: Folklore; the value 11 is a(1) in OEIS A237695 (maximum length of a ±1 sequence of discrepancy n), whose a(2)=1160 is due to B. Konev and A. Lisitsa, A SAT attack on the Erdős discrepancy conjecture, arXiv:1402.2184 (2014)
ladder.note: The case $C=1$ of the Erdős discrepancy problem by hand; the case $C=2$ already needed a SAT solver.

ladder.title: Weyl equidistribution and the quantifier in Khinchin's question
ladder.q:
Let $\alpha$ be irrational. Prove that for every interval $[a,b)\subseteq[0,1)$, $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\#\{1\le k\le n : \{k\alpha\}\in[a,b)\}=b-a.$$

Show on the other hand that for every real $\alpha$ there is a measurable $E\subseteq(0,1)$ with $\lambda(E)=1$ such that $\{k\alpha\}\notin E$ for all $k\ge1$.
ladder.source: H. Weyl, Über die Gleichverteilung von Zahlen mod. Eins, Math. Ann. 77 (1916); L. Kuipers and H. Niederreiter, Uniform Distribution of Sequences, Wiley (1974)
ladder.note: Equidistribution holds for intervals, but no single $\alpha$ works for all measurable sets, so Khinchin's question in Erdős Problem 994 must be read as: for each fixed $E$, for almost all $\alpha$.

ladder.title: Exponential sums of a sequence cannot all stay bounded
ladder.q: Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ be any sequence of real numbers and $e(t)=e^{2\pi it}$. Prove that $$\limsup_{k\to\infty}\ \sup_{n\ge1}\ \Big|\sum_{j=1}^{n}e(kx_j)\Big|=\infty.$$
ladder.source: Remark of P. Erdős (1964), recorded at erdosproblems.com/987 (where it is described as easy), together with the later results of Clunie (1967)
ladder.note: The version with $\sup_n$ is elementary; Erdős Problem 987 asks the same with $\limsup_n$ in place of $\sup_n$, and for the growth rate in $k$.

ladder.title: A multiplicative sequence with logarithmic discrepancy
ladder.q: Let $\lambda:\mathbb{N}\to\{-1,1\}$ be the completely multiplicative function with $\lambda(3)=1$, $\lambda(p)=1$ for primes $p\equiv1\pmod 3$ and $\lambda(p)=-1$ for primes $p\equiv2\pmod 3$. Prove that $$0\le\sum_{k=1}^{n}\lambda(k)\le\log_3 n+1\quad\text{for all } n\ge1,$$ and deduce that $|\sum_{k=1}^{n}\lambda(kd)|\le\log_3 N+1$ whenever $n,d\ge1$ and $nd\le N$.
ladder.source: P. Borwein, S. K. K. Choi and M. Coons, Completely multiplicative functions taking values in {−1,1}, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 362 (2010), 6279–6291 (Corollary 4)
ladder.note: Shows that discrepancy along homogeneous progressions can grow as slowly as $\log N$, matching the lower bound $\gg\log N$ that Erdős conjectured.

ladder.title: Random colourings of pairs: the upper bound n^{3/2}
ladder.q: For $f:\{(x,y): 1\le x<y\le n\}\to\{-1,1\}$ and $X\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ write $f(X)=\sum_{x<y,\ x,y\in X}f(x,y)$. Prove that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every $n\ge1$ some $f$ satisfies $|f(X)|\le Cn^{3/2}$ for all $X\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős (1963), as recorded at erdosproblems.com/1028; the method is the standard Chernoff-plus-union-bound argument, see N. Alon and J. H. Spencer, The Probabilistic Method
ladder.note: Random colouring plus a union bound over all $2^n$ sets gives the upper bound in Erdős Problem 1028.

ladder.title: Roth's theorem on discrepancy in arithmetic progressions
ladder.q: Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that for every $N\ge1$ and every $f:\{1,\ldots,N\}\to\{-1,1\}$ there is an arithmetic progression $P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $$\Big|\sum_{x\in P}f(x)\Big|\ge cN^{1/4}.$$
ladder.source: K. F. Roth, Remark concerning integer sequences, Acta Arith. 9 (1964); the exponent 1/4 is sharp by J. Matoušek and J. Spencer, Discrepancy in arithmetic progressions, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 9 (1996)
ladder.note: For all progressions (not only homogeneous ones) discrepancy is polynomial, in contrast with the logarithmic example above.

ladder.title: Erdős–Spencer lower bound for imbalance of 2-colourings of pairs
ladder.q: With $f(X)$ as above, prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every $f:\{(x,y): 1\le x<y\le n\}\to\{-1,1\}$ there is $X\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|f(X)|\ge cn^{3/2}$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and J. Spencer, Imbalances in k-colorations, Networks 1 (1971/72), 379–385
ladder.note: Matches the random upper bound, giving $H(n)\asymp n^{3/2}$ in Erdős Problem 1028; the density version for large induced subgraphs is Erdős Problem 162.

ladder.title: Spencer's six standard deviations
ladder.q: Prove that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every $n\ge1$ and any $n$ sets $S_1,\ldots,S_n\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there exists $\chi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{-1,1\}$ with $$\Big|\sum_{x\in S_i}\chi(x)\Big|\le C\sqrt n\quad\text{for all } 1\le i\le n.$$
ladder.source: J. Spencer, Six standard deviations suffice, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 289 (1985) (with $C=6$)
ladder.note: Beats random colouring (which gives $\sqrt{2n\log(2n)}$) by partial colouring and entropy; the prototype of all sharp discrepancy bounds.

ladder.title: Law of the iterated logarithm for lacunary exponential sums
ladder.q:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be positive integers with $n_{k+1}/n_k\ge q$ for all $k$, for some fixed $q>1$. Prove that for almost every $\alpha\in[0,1]$, $$\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|\sum_{k=1}^{N}e(n_k\alpha)|}{\sqrt{N\log\log N}}\le1.$$

Deduce that if $f$ is a trigonometric polynomial with $\int_0^1f=0$, then for almost every $\alpha$, $$\sum_{k=1}^{N}f(\{\alpha n_k\})=O\big(\sqrt{N\log\log N}\big),$$ and in particular this sum is $o(N\sqrt{\log\log N})$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and I. S. Gál, On the law of the iterated logarithm I, II, Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Proc. Ser. A 58 = Indag. Math. 17 (1955), 65–76, 77–84 (they prove the limsup equals 1)
ladder.note: Answers Erdős Problem 995 for trigonometric polynomials; the open case is general $f\in L^2$, where Erdős constructed examples whose sums exceed $N(\log\log N)^{1/2-\epsilon}$ infinitely often.

ladder.title: The Erdős discrepancy problem, Hilbert-space form
ladder.q:
Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and $f:\mathbb{N}\to H$ a function with $\|f(n)\|=1$ for all $n$. Prove that $$\sup_{n,d\ge1}\Big\|\sum_{j=1}^{n}f(jd)\Big\|=\infty.$$

In particular, every $f:\mathbb{N}\to\{-1,1\}$ has unbounded discrepancy along homogeneous arithmetic progressions.
ladder.source: T. Tao, The Erdős discrepancy problem, Discrete Analysis 2016:1, arXiv:1509.05363
ladder.note: Reduction to completely multiplicative functions plus a logarithmically averaged Elliott conjecture; the conjectured $\log N$ growth rate remains open.
